chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from some of the truthful ones, who said:

If a man is unable to obtain water but is able to obtain milk, then he should not perform wudu (ablution) with it; rather, it is only water or tayammum. But if he is unable to obtain water and there is nabidh, then I have heard Ḥarīz mention in a hadith that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed wudu (ablution) with nabidh when he could not obtain water.

The first point concerning it is that ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah said: ‘from some of the truthful ones,’ and it is possible that the one to whom he ascribed it was not an Imam; even if he believed him outwardly to be truthful, acting upon it is not obligatory.
The second is that the group has agreed that wudu (ablution) with nabidh is not permissible, so using it as evidence also falls from consideration from this angle.

And even if it were free of all of that, it would be possible to interpret it as referring to water into which a small amount of dates had been placed so that its taste might become pleasant and its salinity and bitterness be reduced, so long as it had not reached a point that stripped it absolutely of the name of water. For nabidh in the language is that in which something has been cast, and water into which a small amount of dates has been placed is called nabidh. And that which indicates this interpretation is what...

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: an Imam, whose authority is central to assessing the report
key_terms.التَّأْوِيلِ: interpretation, used here for reconciling the report linguistically
key_terms.التَّيَمُّمُ: tayammum, the lawful substitute when water is unavailable
key_terms.اللَّبَنِ: milk, mentioned as an invalid substance for wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْعِصَابَةُ: the body of Imami scholars or companions whose consensus is cited
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, the valid basis for wudu (ablution) in this discussion
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification under legal discussion
key_terms.نَبِيذًا: nabidh, a date-infused liquid discussed in relation to wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform wudu (ablution) with nabidh instead of water in Shiʿi fiqh?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the ruling on performing wudu (ablution) when water is unavailable, rejecting milk as a substitute and affirming that the options are water or tayammum. It then examines a report about wudu (ablution) with nabidh, critiques its evidentiary value through sanad/isnad analysis and communal consensus, and finally offers a linguistic interpretation that preserves the substance as still being water.
